discovery: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, including giant TMR in MgO-barrier junctions

nominees.name: Stuart S. P. Parkin
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Microstructure Physics, Halle, Germany

subfield: Condensed matter physics: spintronics and magnetism
motivation: In 1995 Moodera and Miyazaki independently showed large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in ferromagnet/insulator/ferromagnet junctions. This proved that spin-polarized tunnelling could be used in real devices. In 2004 Parkin demonstrated giant TMR through crystalline MgO barriers, alongside the Yuasa group. MgO relies on spin-filtering by the symmetry of the electron states, and it raised magnetoresistance to hundreds of percent. Magnetic tunnel junctions are now the read element in every hard-disk head and the storage cell of commercial MRAM, including today's spin-transfer-torque MRAM embedded in foundry logic processes. They are also the building block of emerging spintronic oscillators and neuromorphic hardware. The 2007 Prize for giant magnetoresistance recognised the birth of spintronics. Tunnel magnetoresistance is the discovery that turned spintronics into a mature, manufacturable technology, and it rests on deep physics of spin-dependent tunnelling.
